It is conjectured in that for any nite subsets A and B of an abelian group, satisfying A \ ( B) = f0g, one has jA _+Bj jAj + jBj 3; prove (or disprove) this conjecture. Solving a problem by Moser, Scherk proved in that if A and B are nite subsets of an abelian group such that A\( B) = f0g, then jA+Bj jAj+jBj 1. (The condition A \ ( B) = f0g means that there is a unique representation of the sort 0 = a + b with a 2 A and b 2 B; speci cally, that with a = b = 0.) The estimate of Scherk's theorem is best possible: equality is attained, for instance, if A and B are arithmetic progressions with the same di erence, the order of which is at least jAj + jBj 1. The conjecture reduces to the special case B A by considering the sets A = A [B and B = A \ B. We have veri ed computationally this case (and hence the general conjecture) for all cyclic groups of order up to 25, and in the case B = A for cyclic groups of order up to 36. The conjecture holds true also for torsion-free abelian groups, for cyclic groups of prime order, and for elementary abelian 2-groups.

evidence.quote: Scherk's theorem for restricted addition. (Cf. [66]) Is there an analog of Scherk's theorem for the restricted sumset A _+B := fa + b: a 2 A; b 2 B; a 6= bg?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $A, B \subseteq G$ be finite nonempty subsets. Define the restricted sumset
$$A \mathbin{\dot{+}} B := \{a + b : a \in A,\ b \in B,\ a \neq b\}.$$
Assume that $A \cap (-B) = \{0\}$; equivalently, the only pair $(a,b) \in A \times B$ with $a + b = 0$ is $(a,b) = (0,0)$.

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses,
$$|A \mathbin{\dot{+}} B| \geq |A| + |B| - 3.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is a restricted-addition analog of Scherk's theorem due to Lev. It is verified for torsion-free groups, cyclic groups of prime order, elementary abelian 2-groups, and computationally for small cyclic groups. Surveys on restricted set addition (Lev, JTNB 2005; recent Kneser-type results for restricted sumsets) describe it as still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Restricted set addition in Abelian groups: results and conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: A system of interrelated conjectures considered as restricted-addition counterparts of classical theorems of Kneser, Kemperman, and Scherk.
status_evidence.claim: The Scherk-type conjecture for restricted sumsets is listed as a conjecture, not a theorem.

status_evidence.title: A Kneser-Type Theorem for Restricted Sumsets (SIAM J. Discrete Math.)
status_evidence.snippet: Lev's problem has been solved for some particular groups and specific subsets, but it remains open for arbitrary groups and arbitrary large subsets.
